items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Norman Schwartz was my manager at the time

ctx.x: [Phil says to his cat] Stop. [Chuckles] That’s my cat. [MN laughs] So, it’s all part of the woof and web of [chuckles] Yeah, so I said, “I gotta get out of here,” and Jill said, “Well, I want to get out of here too.” She was coming off a divorce also. We were both, you know, single and looking to go to the east coast, so. I was actually heading back to Europe since my return to America hadn’t worked out. The year I was in L.A. I made three thousand dollars in that year, you know. I used to make more than that in…

Productions which was Michel Legrand, Nat Shapiro and uh and Norman Schwartz. And we did an album, uh Michel Legrand wrote a thing called “Images” for me and that won a Grammy. And, the, and as irony would have it, I was presented with the award by Benny Goodman – who hated me – as I was on his band in Russia in 1962. In fact, somebody asked Zoot, “What’s it like to tour Russia with Benny Goodman?” and Zoot said, “Any tour with Benny Goodman is like being in Russia,” you know. [both laugh] So, as Benny handed me…
